findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how a pydantic-ai model OBJECT (with `.profile`) is obtained for non-Anthropic providers before `capabilities_for()` is called — either by constructing model objects for all providers before line :341, or by having `capabilities_for()` accept a provider-string fallback for cases where only a string is available.
evidence: runner.py:264: `model = self._model_override or resolved` — for non-Anthropic, `resolved` is a string
runner.py:275: Anthropic-only block `if self._model_override is None and resolved.startswith('anthropic')` replaces model with a real AnthropicModel object; no analogous block for OpenAI/Google
Plan: 'capabilities_for(model) -> ModelCapabilities' reading 'model.profile'

Plan degradation contract: 'A model whose .profile is missing, None, or of an unrecognized type degrades to the conservative record' — this fires for every non-Anthropic string-model, incorrectly returning native_structured_output=False for OpenAI/Google
findings.finding: For non-Anthropic providers (OpenAI, Google), runner.py line 264 leaves `model` as a plain string (e.g. 'openai:gpt-4o') — pydantic-ai constructs the real model object lazily inside Agent(). Calling `capabilities_for(model)` with a string means `getattr(model, 'profile', None)` returns None, triggering the conservative fallback and setting `native_structured_output=False`. This silently breaks OpenAI's and Google's NativeOutput path, which the existing test at test_structured.py:177 will catch as a regression. The plan never specifies how a pydantic-ai model OBJECT is obtained for non-Anthropic providers before capabilities_for() is called.
findings.location: Approach — 'The capability record' section; Scope — runner.py edit targets :341 and :599
scenarios: OpenAI operator uses 'openai:gpt-4o' -> capabilities_for receives a string -> profile=None -> conservative fallback -> native_structured_output=False -> output_mode returns PromptedOutput instead of NativeOutput — silent regression on the primary OpenAI path
Google GLA operator uses 'google-gla:gemini-2.5-flash' -> same failure
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) call `pydantic_ai.models.infer_model(model_string)` (or equivalent) for non-Anthropic providers to materialise a real model object before `capabilities_for()`, or (b) give `capabilities_for()` a two-arg form `capabilities_for(model, resolved_string=None)` that falls back to a string-keyed lookup when `model.profile` is absent — ensuring OpenAI/Google get correct capabilities from their provider prefix rather than the conservative fallback.

findings.finding: AC bullet 7 ('supports_thinking') creates an impossible test scenario that contradicts the override table. The bullet states 'a thinking-capable model with `thinking=False` still gets `NativeOutput` when its profile supports json_schema', but every Claude/Anthropic model — the only thinking-capable Anthropic models — is overridden by `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` to `native_structured_output=False`, which yields `PromptedOutput`, not `NativeOutput`. An implementer reading the AC literally would write a test using an Anthropic thinking model and see it fail. The test can only pass if it uses a non-Anthropic thinking-capable model (e.g. Gemini 2.5 Flash), but the same bullet opens with 'asserted `True` for a thinking-capable Anthropic model', making the subject of the `NativeOutput` assertion ambiguous.
scenarios: Implementer writes the test with an AnthropicModelProfile (Claude), sets thinking=False, expects NativeOutput — test fails because the override forces PromptedOutput.

Implementer writes the test with a Gemini profile (non-Anthropic, thinking-capable) — test passes but the `supports_thinking=True` assertion in the same bullet now uses a non-Anthropic model, contradicting the opening 'thinking-capable Anthropic model' text.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the bullet into two explicit sub-bullets: (a) `supports_thinking` is derived correctly — `True` for a direct `AnthropicModelProfile` (Claude), `False` in the conservative fallback; (b) `output_mode()` does not branch on `supports_thinking` — verified with a **Gemini 2.5 Flash** profile (`supports_thinking=True`, `native_structured_output=True` from profile, no Claude override), `thinking=False` passed, assert `NativeOutput` is returned.
